boundary: 104 candidate search prompts. Numbering and mappings do not establish independent mechanisms, witnessed defects, executable coverage or exhaustiveness.

items.title: Reality
items.prompt: The represented world omits an actual condition capable of changing the required outcome.

items.title: Causality
items.prompt: An observed association or prediction is treated as evidence of the effect of an intervention.

items.title: Possibility
items.prompt: A proposed witness is inadmissible, or the model excludes a genuinely possible situation.

items.title: Values
items.prompt: The chosen success measure does not represent the values governing the intended use.

items.title: Ethics
items.prompt: Technical compliance leaves a consequential ethical obligation outside the evaluated claim.

items.title: Consequences
items.prompt: A correct final result fails to prevent consequential effects during or after execution.

items.title: Stakeholders
items.prompt: A relevant stakeholder or affected group is omitted from requirement formation.

items.title: Purpose
items.prompt: The system solves a well-defined problem different from the intended problem.

items.title: Mission
items.prompt: Local component success is insufficient for the integrated mission outcome.

items.title: Authority
items.prompt: A rule is treated as governing without establishing its issuer, adoption, scope and operative version.

items.title: Intent
items.prompt: The implemented interpretation differs from the independently established intended meaning.

items.title: Communication
items.prompt: Meaning changes between an intended message, its expression, its reception and its use.

items.title: Needs
items.prompt: The stated request is fulfilled while the underlying need remains unmet.

items.title: Objectives
items.prompt: A proxy objective improves while the consequential outcome deteriorates.

items.title: Context
items.prompt: A result is transferred into a setting where its contextual premises no longer hold.

items.title: Boundaries
items.prompt: A guarantee is applied outside its declared system, input, user or operating boundary.

items.title: Environment
items.prompt: An external dependency or operating condition differs from the admitted environment.

items.title: Operating concepts
items.prompt: Actual operational workflows differ from the workflows whose behavior was evaluated.

items.title: Assumptions
items.prompt: A required premise is neither established by the producer nor justified for the application.

items.title: Elicitation
items.prompt: A necessary requirement is never collected from the relevant sources.

items.title: Interpretation
items.prompt: Ambiguous source wording is resolved without authority even though alternatives change the required answer.

items.title: Requirements
items.prompt: The adopted requirement specifies an inadequate, incorrect or irrelevant outcome.

items.title: Requirement derivation
items.prompt: A derived requirement fails to follow from or preserve its governing requirement.

items.title: Requirement allocation
items.prompt: An obligation is assigned to no component or to one lacking the required information or control.

items.title: Requirement validity
items.prompt: An internally precise requirement is unsuitable for the actual intended use.

items.title: Requirement completeness
items.prompt: All declared requirements hold while an essential undeclared requirement is omitted.

items.title: Requirement consistency
items.prompt: Requirements conflict or their combined interpretation creates an unintended gap.

items.title: Acceptance criteria
items.prompt: The acceptance criterion is weaker than the required consequential behavior.

items.title: Language
items.prompt: Syntax or normalization merges expressions that the source language must distinguish.

items.title: Vocabulary and ontology
items.prompt: The same term denotes different kinds of objects across representations.

items.title: Definitions
items.prompt: A familiar name hides a different definition, convention, exception or totalization.

items.title: Typing and identity
items.prompt: Type agreement is used to equate different objects, states, origins or versions.

items.title: Units and reference frames
items.prompt: Numerical values cross a boundary with changed units, epoch, coordinates or physical frame.

items.title: Encoding
items.prompt: Conversion between encodings loses or changes a distinction required by the consumer.

items.title: Abstraction
items.prompt: An abstraction preserves some properties while discarding one required by its actual consumer.

items.title: Models
items.prompt: Model objects, relationships or admitted states fail to represent the relevant system.

items.title: Specifications
items.prompt: The formal specification captures a different or weaker property than the governing specification.

items.title: Contracts
items.prompt: A consumer assumes more than its producer establishes or its interface promises.

items.title: Semantics
items.prompt: The same expression receives different consequential interpretations across components.

items.title: Translation and refinement
items.prompt: A source-to-target transformation lacks the preservation relation required by the claimed refinement.

items.title: Formalization
items.prompt: Formalization changes a relevant quantifier, domain, exception, dependency or object.

items.title: Logical foundations
items.prompt: A result is interpreted outside the logical and foundational assumptions supporting it.

items.title: Axioms
items.prompt: The advertised conclusion conceals a consequential axiom, placeholder or additional assumption.

items.title: Formal statements
items.prompt: The theorem's actual type differs from its name or advertised mathematical conclusion.

items.title: Proof obligations
items.prompt: A necessary producer-to-consumer bridge is omitted, assumed or left without a discharged supplier.

items.title: Proof construction
items.prompt: The proof establishes an intermediate result without completing the required implication to the target.

items.title: Proof checking
items.prompt: Elaborator completion, a displayed declaration or a partial check is mistaken for accepted exact-target proof.

items.title: Trusted computing base
items.prompt: An unexamined or faulty trusted dependency compromises the stated verification boundary.

items.title: Proof adequacy
items.prompt: A valid proof establishes a proposition too weak to imply the external requirement.

items.title: Architecture
items.prompt: The architecture leaves an obligation unenforced or the needed information unavailable.

items.title: Design
items.prompt: A local design choice creates an integrated inconsistency or uncovered case.

items.title: Algorithms
items.prompt: The algorithm violates its contract on exceptional inputs, boundary cases or resource conditions.

items.title: Interfaces
items.prompt: Adjacent components disagree about identity, lengths, ownership, nullability, ordering or errors.

items.title: Implementation
items.prompt: The executed implementation differs from the algorithm or model whose properties were established.

items.title: Build and dependency resolution
items.prompt: The build selects the wrong source, dependency, generated artifact, cache or baseline binary.

items.title: Configuration and deployment
items.prompt: Deployment changes a configuration or environmental premise on which qualification depended.

items.title: Runtime behavior
items.prompt: Scheduling, callbacks, cancellation, timing or resource effects alter the required executed behavior.

items.title: Physical effects
items.prompt: A computed or simulated result is applied to physical behavior without a sufficient empirical bridge.

items.title: Test oracle
items.prompt: The criterion for the expected answer is incorrect, incomplete or improperly grounded.

items.title: Test execution
items.prompt: Tests skip the intended behavior, execute the wrong artifact or pass for the wrong reason.

items.title: Observation and measurement
items.prompt: Measurement uses the wrong channel, interval, resolution or proxy for the protected property.

items.title: Evidence and provenance
items.prompt: A result lacks a reliable connection to its exact source, input, execution, tool and claim.

items.title: Claims and warrants
items.prompt: A conclusion exceeds its evidence's strength, domain, authority or applicability.

items.title: Authorization, decisions and learning
items.prompt: Evidence is converted into an unauthorized decision or retained after its governing basis changes.

items.title: Identity
items.prompt: A matching name, type, label or signature is mistaken for exact subject identity.

items.title: Distinction
items.prompt: The representation fails to separate admitted cases requiring incompatible decisions.

items.title: Equivalence
items.prompt: A claimed equivalence fails to preserve the protected property or permitted-answer compatibility.

items.title: Scope
items.prompt: Evidence is extended beyond the cases, premises, users or consequences it covers.

items.title: Completeness of representation
items.prompt: Relevant state or structure cannot be expressed in the representation used for checking.

items.title: Information loss
items.prompt: A transformation erases a difference that changes the protected requirement.

items.title: Ambiguity
items.prompt: Several readings or derivations are admitted while a guarantee silently relies on only one.

items.title: Vacuity
items.prompt: An empty domain, impossible premise, unreachable branch or trivial conclusion makes a check uninformative.

items.title: Observability
items.prompt: Available observations cannot distinguish admissible situations requiring incompatible decisions.

items.title: Oracle independence
items.prompt: The reference oracle shares the source, assumptions or interpretation it is intended to challenge.

items.title: Common-mode failure
items.prompt: A shared cause makes multiple checks or components agree on the same wrong result.

items.title: Counterfactual behavior
items.prompt: The evidence never examines the outcome when a consequential condition changes or fails.

items.title: Sensitivity
items.prompt: The detector stays positive under a relevant mutation that should defeat its claimed guarantee.

items.title: Uncertainty
items.prompt: Unsupported, unknown, inconclusive, false and verified outcomes are conflated.

items.title: Temporal validity
items.prompt: Evidence is treated as applicable after its qualifying conditions cease to hold.

items.title: Change propagation
items.prompt: A changed dependency fails to trigger withdrawal or requalification of affected claims.

items.title: Supersession
items.prompt: A prior result remains controlling after an applicable correction or replacement.

items.title: Reproducibility
items.prompt: The declared materials and procedure do not reconstruct the reported result.

items.title: Independence of evidence
items.prompt: Evidence items with a shared origin or failure cause are counted as independent corroboration.

items.title: Adversarial robustness
items.prompt: A guarantee fails for malformed, adversarial or strategically selected admissible inputs.

items.title: Security and trust boundaries
items.prompt: Untrusted metadata, callbacks or receipts are accepted as self-authenticating evidence or authority.

items.title: Permission and legitimacy
items.prompt: Technical capability or evidential confidence is mistaken for permission to act.

items.title: Incentives
items.prompt: The reward structure favors proxy success or selected evidence over the consequential objective.

items.title: Accountability
items.prompt: Responsibility for a requirement, interpretation, decision or correction is not established.

items.title: Risk and reversibility
items.prompt: Evidence adequate for a reversible trial is used to authorize a higher-consequence irreversible action.

items.title: Evidence transport
items.prompt: A result is transferred to another representation or system without the needed applicability bridge.

items.title: Composition
items.prompt: Individually valid component guarantees fail to supply one another's required premises.

items.title: Emergence
items.prompt: Interactions produce relevant behavior absent from the isolated component models.

items.title: Human interpretation
items.prompt: A human reading strengthens or changes a checked claim by losing an exception, quantifier or operation.

items.title: Institutional interpretation
items.prompt: Review, merge, publication or institutional approval is interpreted beyond its actual remit.

items.title: Environmental drift
items.prompt: External operating conditions change while the assurance basis remains fixed.

items.title: Unknown unknowns
items.prompt: A finite checklist or model is treated as proof that all consequential failure possibilities are represented.

items.title: Numerics
items.prompt: Precision, rounding, overflow, exceptional values or tolerances change the mathematical claim being relied upon.

items.title: Statistical inference
items.prompt: Selection, base rates, multiplicity, optional stopping, survivorship or miscalibrated uncertainty overstate an empirical conclusion.

items.title: Liveness and termination
items.prompt: Required progress or termination is unproved or fails; safety checks do not establish it, and fairness premises may be unjustified.

items.title: Fault handling and recovery
items.prompt: Error propagation, partial failure, degraded operation, retry, recovery or rollback violates the applicable behavioral contract.

items.title: Input coverage
items.prompt: The selected inputs omit a relevant region while results are generalized to the full claimed domain.

items.title: Legal, regulatory and privacy obligations
items.prompt: Applicable legal, regulatory, privacy, consent or licensing duties are omitted or assigned the wrong scope.

items.title: Maintenance and evolution
items.prompt: Accumulated internal changes, deprecation or knowledge loss undermine applicability or the ability to reestablish a supported claim.

items.title: Value
items.prompt: Additional assurance work fails to improve the independently specified decision outcome or its fully measured cost.
